title: They were clapping for them…
paragraphs:
They were clapping for them…
while God was watching you.

And suddenly—
the noise got quiet.

Not outside.
Inside.

Because comparison is loud…
but conviction whispers.

You see the polished lives.
The applause.
The “perfect” works.

Their ministry.
Their success.
Their highlight reels dressed like holiness.
And something inside you tightens.

“Why not me?”
“Am I behind?”
“Am I enough?”
But listen carefully, brother… sister…
God is not grading your life on their paper.
“But let every man prove his own work…” — Galatians 6:4 (KJV)

Paul didn’t say compare.
He didn’t say compete.
He said prove.

Test it.
Examine it.
Lay your life bare before God.
Not before people.

Because you can impress a crowd…
and still fail the presence of God.

You can receive applause…
and still lack obedience.

You can build something visible…
and still be empty inside.
Jesus said it like this:
“For what is a man profited, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul?” — Matthew 16:26
Read that again.

You can win out there…
and lose in here.
But here’s what we miss—

God is not asking for perfection.
He’s asking for truth.

Not a perfect work.
A proven heart.
“Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves.” — 2 Corinthians 13:5
This is not condemnation.
This is invitation.
Look at your life.

Not filtered.
Not edited.
Not compared.
Just… honest.

Are you walking with Him…
or just performing for them?

Are you obeying His voice…
or chasing their validation?

Are you building something eternal…
or just something visible?

Because one day—
everything will be tested.

Not by likes.
Not by followers.
Not by applause.
By fire.
“Every man’s work shall be made manifest… the fire shall try every man’s work of what sort it is.” — 1 Corinthians 3:13
Fire doesn’t lie.
It reveals.
And suddenly…

Your secret prayers matter more than public platforms.
Your quiet obedience outweighs loud recognition.
Your hidden surrender becomes eternal reward.
But wait—don’t miss this…
This is where grace walks in.

Because if you’re honest right now…
you’ll realize:
Your work isn’t perfect.

Your motives have cracks.
Your obedience has gaps.
Your heart has wandered.
And if it’s all up to your work—
You’re in trouble.
So am I.
But the Gospel…
Oh, the Gospel.

Jesus didn’t come for perfect workers.
He came for broken sinners.
“But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.” — Romans 5:8

Before you could prove anything—
He already proved His love.
At the cross.
That distant shadow you see…
That man carrying the wood…
That’s not just history.
That’s your hope.

Because while your work is being tested—
Jesus already finished the work that saves you.
“It is finished.” — John 19:30
So now—

We don’t prove our work to earn salvation.
We prove our work because we have salvation.

Not for approval.
But from acceptance.
So stop measuring yourself by them.
Start surrendering yourself to Him.

Let God examine your life—
not to destroy you…
but to refine you.
“Search me, O God, and know my heart: try me, and know my thoughts.” — Psalm 139:23
Here’s the truth that will set you free:
You don’t need to be better than them.
You need to be faithful to Him.

And when your work is proven—
not perfect, but surrendered—
There will be a quiet joy.

Not loud.
Not flashy.
But real.
“…then shall he have rejoicing in himself alone, and not in another.” — Galatians 6:4
Because your peace will no longer depend on comparison.
It will come from communion.
So pause.
Right now.
Ask yourself:

If God examined my life today…
what would remain?
And if that question convicts you—
Good.
That means grace is calling.
Come back to Jesus.

Not polished.
Not pretending.
Just real.

Because the same God who tests your work…
is the same Savior who redeems your heart.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
